subject: Proposal: tiered overrun charging + fair-use buffer for Dedicated commits
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@acme.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated commit questions — handling bursts above reserved GPU pools

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Dedicated product looks promising. Before we move to a commit, procurement has asked for clearer language and numbers on what happens if our usage exceeds the reserved GPU pool. A few specific asks:

- How is excess usage metered? Is it per-GPU-hour, per-token, or via a blended estimate?
- Do you throttle or queue requests when the pool is saturated? Any SLA/latency guarantees when over-commit occurs?
- Are there caps or automated credits if we see a big spike (e.g., 2–3x baseline for a few hours)?
- Can you provide an example invoice calculation for a sample month where committed capacity is 40 GPU-hours/day and peak demand briefly hits 120 GPU-hours/day?

We’ve attached a small June snapshot of our expected profile. Happy to hop on a call if it’s easier.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme AI
procurement@acme.ai

Attachments: acme_usage_snapshot_June2026.csv (CSV, 42KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit questions — handling bursts above reserved GPU pools

Emily — thanks for the clear list. I’ve sketched a short proposal below that we can formalize into contract language. High level summary first, then the invoice example.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Metering: primary metering is per-GPU-hour (or per vGPU-equivalent-hour) for Dedicated; token-metering applies for hosted APIs only. We translate model profiles to GPU-hour consumption at portfolio-level (we include the mapping in the attached PDF).
- Overrun approach: we offer a tiered overrun charge + a small "fair-use buffer" that lets short spikes be absorbed without immediate billing at peak rates.
- Throttling: by default we will not throttle production traffic; we will attempt to honor requests with fallbacks to lower-cost model variants or cross-region routing when available. If sustained usage > 150% of commit for 24+ hours and capacity is constrained, automated throttling can be applied as a last resort (we will notify and provide mitigation options).
- Credits: for one-off measurement anomalies or platform incidents, we provide invoice-level credits (not automatic) — we can pre-agree a credit window in the MSA.

Example invoice (monthly):
Baseline: committed 40 GPU-hours/day => 1,200 GPU-hours/month (flat commit price: $X per GPU-hour in your tier).
Observed: 120 GPU-hours/day peak for 3 days (spike) + 40 GPU-hours/day otherwise => total observed 1,560 GPU-hours/month.
Overrun breakdown: first 10% overcommit = billed at 1.15x committed rate (buffer absorption). Next 40% = billed at 1.5x committed rate. Anything beyond that billed at 2.0x committed rate.
Sample calc (numbers illustrative):
- Committed charge: 1,200 * $8 = $9,600
- Overrun units: 360 GPU-hours total overcommit
  - 10% buffer (120 GPU-hours) billed at 1.15x => 120 * $9.2 = $1,104
  - next 40% (144 GPU-hours) billed at 1.5x => 144 * $12 = $1,728
  - remaining (96 GPU-hours) billed at 2.0x => 96 * $16 = $1,536
Total month charge = $9,600 + $1,104 + $1,728 + $1,536 = $13,968

I attached a short PDF that formalizes the tiers and includes a few variants (monthly lookback windows, daily vs hourly metering). Can you confirm whether Acme prefers per-hour granularity or a daily-aggregated lookback? That choice changes the exposure profile.

If that sounds reasonable I can loop in contracts/finance and provide a cleaned version for your procurement team.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_tiered_overrun_v1.pdf (PDF, 24 pages)

From: Emily Park <emily.park@acme.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit questions — handling bursts above reserved GPU pools

Karthik — this is helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and infra engineering: 

1) We prefer an hourly metering granularity (so we can model short bursts) but want a guaranteed daily throughput floor (e.g., at least 90% of committed/day before overrun tiers apply). Is that something you support?
2) For the fair-use buffer, can we make the first 5%/day free (absorbed) and the next 15%/day at 1.1x, with remaining billed as you suggested? That softens the tail exposure for sudden jobs.
3) On throttling: if Redwood enacts automated throttling due to sustained over-commit, can you commit to a 2-hour notice window and a defined rollback plan (e.g., duration-limited throttles with explanation and contact path)?

Also — procurement asked whether we can structure the overrun buckets as dollar caps rather than multipliers. We're open to either but need firm max exposure per month as part of the SOW.

Happy to take a 30-minute call to finalize.

Emily

Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: pricing and credit ops notes for Acme negotiation

Looping internal notes into the thread so procurement has visibility:

- Marissa (pricing) proposes an alternate structure: hourly metering + a rolling 7-day lookback for spike smoothing. That prevents a single large job from triggering the top-tier multiplier immediately.
- Vivek (ops) requests the following SLA language if we agree to minimal throttling: 2-hour notice, throttles limited to non-blocking degradation (best-effort retries), and automated fallback to a pre-approved model variant. Also wants telemetry hooks and a playbook link included.
- We can accept a soft dollar cap option: e.g., allow Acme to set a monthly overrun cap of $25k; if projected monthly overrun would exceed that cap, we'll notify and stop billing beyond cap until they authorize an overage release. That meets procurement's ask for max exposure.

Action items I recommend before call:
- Karthik: prepare two sample invoices (hourly lookback, 7-day smoothing) with dollar-cap variants.
- Vivek: prepare a 1-page ops playbook describing throttle flow, notification channels, and fallback model list.
- Marissa: draft SOW paragraph for tiered overrun + dollar cap option.

Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: tiered overrun charging + fair-use buffer for Dedicated commits — next steps

Emily / team — thanks for the quick turn. Per our internal notes we’ll do the following for the SOW and next-touch: 

1) Metering: hourly granularity, with a 7-day rolling smoothing window (preferred for spikes). We’ll include an option to instead use a daily aggregation at your request.
2) Fair-use buffer: default 5% free absorption per day; next 15% billed at 1.1x, next 30% at 1.5x, remainder at 2.0x. We’ll include a dollar-cap toggle — you can specify a monthly overrun cap (example: $25k) which prevents billing beyond that threshold unless you explicitly approve further overage.
3) Throttling: automated throttles reserved for sustained >150% commit for 24+ hours. For shorter events, we will try fallbacks (lower-cost model variants, cross-region routing). If throttling is required we will provide a minimum 2-hour notice and a rollback plan; Vivek will supply the playbook.
4) Credits & incidents: invoice credits for platform incidents will be handled via support tickets; we can pre-define a credit window and thresholds in the MSA.

Next steps: I’ll schedule a 30-minute call to run the sample invoices and get confirmation on the dollar-cap value. Marissa will circulate two sample invoices (hourly vs 7-day smoothing) and Vivek will attach the ops playbook. If that works, procurement can accept the SOW paragraph and we’ll route to contracts.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
